pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: The front door lets the owner's phone on the tailnet reach a bearings tier: it binds the box's Tailscale IPv4 on the tier's port and pipes every connection to the loopback page service, with no root, no header rewriting, and no change to the page process.
purpose.is-not: It is not a proxy that reads HTTP, not TLS, and not a public ingress; the command center's public door at map.gatehouse.click is G6's (N-35) and lives on the cluster.
purpose.why: PR 186 taught the page to accept the tailnet Host names but nothing listened on the tailnet address; tailscale serve needs root and a password the owner will not type; PR 187 shipped a dependency-free forwarder in a herdr pane. This node carries that forwarder as a supervised unit, which is the current state the brief names.
purpose.decisions: D08 every system process its own supervised unit (C46), D22 display on the WSL host (C38), map-hosting-and-feel-rules (the owner wants the factory in his pocket), no-bureaucracy-creep (a card cannot be answered from a page he cannot reach).

input.text: The unit starts with its tier (BindsTo the page unit) and binds only after page.up for its page is in the store, or after it can connect to the loopback port, whichever is first; a door with nothing behind it would answer the phone with a reset, which is worse than no door.

record.field: the tier's port (stable 44900; the phone URL uses the same port as the loopback link)
the tailnet names the page accepts for this bind (from allowed_hosts), so a reader can print the phone URL without the key
EADDRINUSE, EADDRNOTAVAIL (the Tailscale IP changed), or no bind address found
a second start while the lock names a live pid; exit 3
the Tailscale IP changed; the unit exits 0 to be restarted on the new address
stop (100) or crash (500, written by N-06)

mechanism.where: Go subcommand coq-bearings front-door --page <page> in the control plane module (a port of tools/bearings/scripts/front-door.mjs, same behaviour, one language), run as the systemd user unit instance coq-front-door@<page>.service on the WSL host.
mechanism.step: Resolve the tier and page from tools/bearings/config/bearings.json; read the target port from ${COQ_STATE}/bearings/<page>/server.json (or the tier's fixed port); find the bind address: --bind or BEARINGS_FRONT_DOOR_BIND, else tailscale ip -4 (5 s timeout), else config front_door.bind, else exit 3 with front-door.failed naming no bind address.
Lock: ${COQ_STATE}/bearings/<page>/front-door.json {pid, bind, port, at}; a live pid in it is front-door.refused 409 and exit 3 (RestartPreventExitStatus=3); an unreadable lock is logged and ignored.

Wait for the back end: connect to 127.0.0.1:<target_port> with a 2 s timeout, up to 3 tries 2 s apart; if it never answers, exit 1 with front-door.failed reason backend, and systemd retries after RestartSec (the page unit is what is wrong, and BindsTo stops this unit when the page unit stops).
Bind <bind>:<port>; 3 tries 2 s apart (retry_ms); then exit 4 with front-door.failed. On success write the lock, write front-door 100, log one line.

Forward: for every accepted connection open a loopback connection and pipe both ways; errors on either side drop both; no byte is inspected or changed, so the phone's Host header reaches the page as sent and passes allowed_hosts (PR 186). Connections are counted for the health line.

IP watch: every 60 s run tailscale ip -4 (5 s timeout); if it differs from the bound address, write front-door.rebind 100 and exit 0 so systemd restarts the unit on the new address (Restart=always covers exit 0 too). This closes the cost noted in PR 187 (a restart when the Tailscale IP changes) with no human.
Stop: SIGTERM closes the listener, drops live connections after a 5 s drain, removes the lock, writes front-door.down 100, exit 0.
mechanism.text: Why a forwarder and not binding the page to the tailnet address: the page process stays on loopback with one listener and one auth path, and a change of address never restarts the page or its watch (PR 187 breadcrumb, rejected list).

unit.name: coq-front-door@.service
unit.line: [Unit] Description=coq bearings tailnet front door for %i; BindsTo=coq-bearings@%i.service; After=coq-bearings@%i.service tailscaled.service network-online.target; StartLimitIntervalSec=0

[Service] Type=simple; ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/coq-bearings front-door --page %i; Restart=always; RestartSec=10; RestartPreventExitStatus=3; MemoryMax=64M; Environment=COQ_STATE=%h/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin

start.text: Enabled for stable once by the install script; BindsTo and WantedBy tie it to the page unit, so a tier that comes up gets its door and a tier that goes down loses it, with no verb to type. uat and dev tiers get a door only when tools/bearings/config/bearings.json tiers.<tier>.front_door is true (stable true, others false by default: the owner confirms uat pages from the desktop or by explicit config).

wait.fallback: config front_door.bind; then exit 3 with the reason
exit 1 front-door.failed backend; systemd retries after 10 s; BindsTo stops it if the page unit is gone
exit 4 front-door.failed; systemd retries after 10 s; three failures in 5 min is an unhealthy record (N-06) and an alert on N-41, because the owner's phone cannot reach the page

wait.timeout: TCP keepalive 30 s idle; no application timeout (SSE streams are long-lived by design)
wait.fallback: a dead peer is dropped by keepalive; the page's SSE client reconnects
a failed check keeps the current bind; three failed checks in a row log once; an address change restarts within 60 s

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node was a human restarting a pane after a Tailscale IP change. Timeout: the 60 s watch. Fallback: exit and restart by systemd. The owner never finds the door closed without the alerts screen saying so first.

retries.rule: Bind and back end connect retry 3 times then exit with a record; systemd is the process-level retry at 10 s; every failure is a front-door.failed record that N-06 counts and N-41 shows.

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume.
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets touch the front-door subcommand, tools/bearings/units/coq-front-door@.service and the install script; nothing else.

collision.what: two front doors for one tier

many-agents-at-once.collision: The lock file with a live pid refuses the second (409, exit 3), and the bind itself fails with EADDRINUSE for anything that slips past the lock; one door per tier is the kernel's rule as much as ours.
Different ports, so one bind address carries both; the config says which tiers have a door.

collision.what: the page restarts while the door is up

many-agents-at-once.collision: BindsTo restarts the door with the page; live phone connections drop and the phone's EventSource reconnects by itself (N-31), landing on the new page instance.

collision.what: two devices on the tailnet at once

many-agents-at-once.collision: Each is its own forwarded connection; the door has no shared state per client.
many-agents-at-once.test: tests start two door processes for one page in the Podman harness with a fake tailscale binary: the second exits 3; a changed fake IP yields front-door.rebind and a new bind within one watch interval; a killed back end yields front-door.failed backend and a restart.

N-06 counts; N-41 alert; N-52 push when live

path.what: one line per start, stop, rebind, failure; never a key, never a URL with a key

edges.out: the tailnet URL (no DAG node; the owner is the sink)
edges.lamp: front door state on the Controls screen

security.rule: Plain HTTP between the phone and the box inside the WireGuard-encrypted tailnet; no TLS of its own; the page's key plus HttpOnly cookie is the auth, and the Host allow-list names the tailnet names and address only (whoadudette-1, whoadudette-1.tailef6830.ts.net, 100.122.200.108).

The key is never in a record, a log, a push or this volume; the phone URL with the key is printed by coq owner url to the operator's terminal only, and the owner's first open sets the cookie so later links carry no key (N-52 relies on this).
The door listens on the Tailscale address only, never 0.0.0.0; a config bind outside 100.64.0.0/10 is refused with exit 3 (CGNAT range check), so a typo can never open the page to the LAN.
security.cost: One more process per tier with a door (about 8 MB); a 60 s window after an IP change; a restart of the door on every page restart.
security.later: With root once, sudo tailscale serve --bg --http=80 http://127.0.0.1:44900 gives port 80 and needs no door process; kept as the alternative, not taken, because the owner wants no sudo step (PR 187).

item.proof: systemctl --user is-active coq-front-door@coq-stable; store holds front-door 100 with bind 100.122.200.108 and port 44900

permissions.runs-as: the owner user, no sudo, MemoryMax 64M; may run tailscale ip -4 (read-only, no root needed)
permissions.may: bind the Tailscale address on the tier's port; connect to loopback; write its lock and its records
permissions.may-not: read or alter traffic; bind any other address; touch the page's state beyond its own lock; run tailscale serve
